question: The supplement of an angle is 3 times its complement. How many degrees is the angle?
solution: Let the angle measure \(x^\circ\). Then \(180-x=3(90-x)\), which gives \(x=45\).

solutionMethods.explanation: The supplement and complement are found by subtracting the same angle from \(180^\circ\) and \(90^\circ\), so their difference is \(180^\circ-90^\circ=90^\circ\). The supplement is three copies of the complement, so this difference is two copies of the complement. Therefore the complement measures \(90^\circ\div2=45^\circ\), and the angle measures \(90^\circ-45^\circ=45^\circ\).
solutionMethods.label: Use the 90° difference

reference.question: The supplement of an angle is 3 times its complement. How many degrees is the angle?
reference.solution:
Method 1: Set up an angle equation

Let the angle measure \(x^\circ\). Then \(180-x=3(90-x)\), which gives \(x=45\).

Method 2: Use the 90° difference

The supplement and complement are found by subtracting the same angle from \(180^\circ\) and \(90^\circ\), so their difference is \(180^\circ-90^\circ=90^\circ\). The supplement is three copies of the complement, so this difference is two copies of the complement. Therefore the complement measures \(90^\circ\div2=45^\circ\), and the angle measures \(90^\circ-45^\circ=45^\circ\).
